Selection sort, step by step

Selection sort finds the smallest value in the unsorted part and swaps it to the front of that part. After each pass the sorted part grows by one.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. Point min at the first unsorted value.
  2. Compare every later value with min. When one is smaller, point min at it.
  3. Swap the value at min to the front of the unsorted part. It is now sorted.
  4. Repeat until one value is left.

Cost

Time
O(n²) compares in every case, but at most n − 1 swaps.
Space
O(1): it sorts in place.
Stable
No: the swap can jump a value past an equal one.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain selection sort with stepthru tracer calls, such as compare and pointer, that record each step.
